school: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
program: Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (BCB) PhD (via BBSP)

requirements.quote: The BCB PhD and certificate programs do not have formal prerequisites as such.
students with no experience of calculus are strongly advised to acquire basic calculus skills before attempting courses that assume it
In general, recent practice with calculus and experience with at least one programming language (not necessarily any of those listed above) will be a strong advantage.
familiarity with or willingness to learn basic matrix algebra
students who have never programmed before are encouraged to gain practice programming in at least one language before attempting courses that have a programming component
typically competitive applications show coursework and/or experience in both biological/chemical/biomedical science and quantitative subjects.
Ideal BCB candidates should have an undergraduate degree in a biological, physical, mathematical, or computational science.

problems: No formal prerequisites; guidance is tied to first-year core courses: BCB 720 Introduction to Statistical Modeling 'assumes single variable calculus at least up to Calc 1' plus familiarity with or willingness to learn basic matrix algebra and R; BCB 715 assumes familiarity with calculus (differentiation).
BBSP umbrella (bbsp.unc.edu apply / course-requirements pages) states no math coursework: 'We welcome applicants with a background in a biological, chemical, or physical science.'
